subject: [AMBER] Is it possible to create a deb for ubuntu or a pypi one ?

messages.author: aishen.free.fr
messages.body:
Hi,
After trying to compile amber20 on ubuntu it still doesn't work , now
it's problem with mini conda python which doesn't give numpy scipy
matplotlib, I don't want to lose time using conda it's doing a big mess
even on window at the time. All both system were working fine and few
days ago nothing worked any more after looking at the problem it's
anaconda which changed python version !
If possible would be nice otherwise I can't use anymore amber20 and it's
a shade.
Kind regards
Henri

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Mar 28, 2021, aishen.free.fr wrote:
>
>After trying to compile amber20 on ubuntu it still doesn't work , now
>it's problem with mini conda python which doesn't give numpy scipy
>matplotlib,
Did you use the default, and ask Amber to download a miniconda for you?
That procedure will (a) provide scipy and matplotlib, and (b) not interfere with
any other python you have in your system.
>All both system were working fine and few
>days ago nothing worked any more after looking at the problem it's
>anaconda which changed python version !
You may need to check you PATH variable:  If you don't wish to use the
python that Amber installs, make sure it is not the first one in your $PATH.
We'll try to help more if you can provide details about what choices you
made in installing Amber20, and what the details of the problem are are.
...dac

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Mon, Mar 29, 2021, Hrishikesh Dhondge wrote:
>
>I was also having some issues with the compilation. Have you tried to
>compile with superuser access?
>For me, it worked when I tried as a superuser from my system. Hope it helps!
Just a note that we (Amber developers) encourage people *not* to make use of
superuser privleges.  They are not needed if you install in a location where
you have write access.
We are not aware of any dangerous glitches in the installation scripts, but
the procedure is quite involved, and some steps depend on the environment
that is found.  You are exposing yourself to extra risks by installing as a
superuser.
There are cases where a superuser approach is appropriate, but they are not
common.
....dac
